raw.assessment: Full assembly plausibly provides a physical completeness check and a starting arrangement, while retaining rearrangeability; these benefits are hypotheses. Recorded absence of damage supports retaining current packaging provisionally. Performance remains short of the time target, with only seven of ten observed customers succeeding unaided. Five component complaints suggest a contents problem but do not establish five verified packing errors. The concrete limiting observation is that both workers finish repeated three-compartment orders in seven to nine minutes: assembly is not uniformly slow. All six extreme delays occurred in mixed batches, but layout complexity and switching remain confounded. Overlapping partition widths likewise do not identify the cause of insertion retries.

openings.claim: Order switching during selection and checking may explain part of the mixed-batch delay and contents errors; staging one complete order together before insertion may help.
openings.delta: Localizes a potentially avoidable cost within the incumbent assembled workflow.
openings.prediction: For comparable layouts, staging reduces selection/checking time and discrepancies while insertion time remains similar. If insertion dominates instead, this account weakens.
openings.probe: Use existing spare-board samples for paired builds under current selection versus one-order staging, alternating sequence and balancing workers and layout counts. Log selection, insertion, checking and packing separately, plus required-part discrepancies. Reuse a bench area; keep dimensions, parts, colors and packaging unchanged.
assumptions: Bench staging fits the available space without blocking the other worker.
Sample work fits existing delivery slack; do not delay accepted orders.

openings.claim: The generic three-layout diagram may leave the short partition's ordered position ambiguous even when all correct parts are supplied.
openings.delta: Separates instruction ambiguity from missing parts and insertion difficulty.
openings.prediction: An order-specific diagram reduces short-partition questions and unaided arrangement failures despite identical, verified contents.
openings.probe: Randomly assign ten willing participants to current or order-specific diagrams using verified sample organizers. Record first-exposure arrangement success, short-partition questions and insertion failures. Treat this small comparison as directional evidence.
assumptions: Diagram preparation and reproduction stay within the initial 500 and recurring 0.40 limits and the fixed delivery date.
Ordered counts, colors, capacity, footprint and detachable construction are retained.

raw.assessment: D2-O5 is awkward: widths overlap between first-attempt and second-attempt partitions, weakening a width-only account. D2-O6 confounds complexity with switching. These competing hypotheses establish neither pilot success nor the cause of missing-part reports.

openings.claim: Layout switching disrupts remembered placement and insertion sequence. Repetition stabilizes that sequence; unfamiliar transitions produce searches or premature insertions even with ordinary-width parts.
openings.delta: Links repetition speed and the width anomaly through sequence interference; customer short-part uncertainty is compatible evidence.
openings.prediction: For the same target layout and prechecked components, attempts immediately following a different layout show more placement corrections and longer insertion time than repeated-layout attempts; a layout-specific sequence cue reduces that transition penalty.
openings.probe: Reuse 12 spare-board samples across both probes. Both workers assemble identical target layouts in counterbalanced repeated and alternating sequences, with and without a handwritten sequence cue. Time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately; count placement corrections and second attempts. Stable troublesome joints would weaken this account.
assumptions: Brief bench trials fit available time without delaying accepted orders.
Existing slips and tools suffice within both cost caps; delivered dimensions, capacity, colors, compartment counts and removable joints remain unchanged.

openings.claim: Unmeasured slot condition or joint alignment creates difficult part-slot pairings despite overlapping partition widths. Repeated three-compartment layouts may encounter fewer such pairings; mixed batches may contain layouts that expose them.
openings.delta: Explains overlapping widths through local joint properties; mixed-batch delay could reflect layout composition.
openings.prediction: Second attempts cluster at particular slots or pairings and persist with correct placement cues, regardless of the preceding layout.
openings.probe: Using the same samples, exchange matched-width partitions among compatible slots and repeat with controlled insertion order, recording pair identity, visible edge condition and attempt number. Counterbalance repetitions to detect wear. Slot-following failures support local slot effects; transition-following failures favor A1.
assumptions: Compatible exchanges preserve the ordered geometry and stationery capacity.
Sample reuse and recording fit the same time and cost envelope; accepted products require no modification.

openings.claim: Switching may disrupt selection/checking or placement/insertion sequence.
openings.discriminator: Staging reduces selection/checking time and discrepancies; sequence cues reduce transition-specific insertion corrections.
openings.probe: Reuse 12 samples; counterbalance both workers and comparable layouts across current/staged selection, repeated/alternating layouts and cue/no cue. Log each work stage, discrepancies, corrections and retries.
openings.uncertainty: Complexity confounds switching; bench space and delivery slack remain unverified.

openings.claim: Generic diagrams may obscure the short partition’s ordered position despite correct contents.
openings.discriminator: Order-specific diagrams improve unaided success and reduce questions with identical verified contents.
openings.probe: Randomly assign ten participants to current/order-specific diagrams; record first-exposure success, questions and insertion failures.
openings.uncertainty: Small comparison is directional; complaints do not establish verified packing errors.

openings.claim: Slot condition or alignment may create difficult pairings despite overlapping widths.
openings.discriminator: Retries persist at particular slots/pairings despite cues and regardless of preceding layout.
openings.probe: Reuse samples; exchange matched-width parts among compatible slots with controlled insertion order. Record pairing, edge condition and attempts; counterbalance repetitions for wear.
openings.uncertainty: Widths do not establish cause; transition-following failures favor D1 sequence interference.

lineage.reason: Selection/checking mechanism preserved separately from insertion sequencing.
Sequence interference and cue discriminator preserved.

post_distill.decision: Probe before adoption; synthetic observations establish no pilot success. Preserve 30×20 cm footprint, capacity, removable joints, accepted counts/colors and fixed delivery; require ≤500 initial and ≤0.40/order. Retain packaging provisionally. Full assembly’s completeness and starting-arrangement benefits remain hypotheses.
